review.summary: approve_with_nits. Fact preservation holds: every identifier and number traced from removed prose reappears in an API details table; chart values recompute. Link checker clean on the notes (6 failures, all in REVIEW.md, outside this diff); pytest blocked by a missing review-harness fixture; diagram previews could not render here. Top findings: (1) 6.4 still calls 5.5's traces "layer-5" after the PR fixed 7.1 for the same error; (2) Week 5 review says adaptive attacks "beat every published detector" while 5.4 says "most"; (3) error-two-paths diagram routes every in-tool failure through "retry inside the tool", which the lesson calls a mistake for task errors.

findings.checklist_item: Flow: when a lesson says "layer N", name it too; A. Contradictions between lessons
findings.title: 6.4 calls 5.5's traces "layer-5" after the PR corrected the same error in 7.1
findings.claim: 6.4 'Where it lives' now reads "computed from the traces of 5.5 (the layer-5 traces)". Lesson 5.5 says observability "is layer 6 (feedback and evals)", and the PR description says it corrected 7.1 for placing observability in layer 5. 6.4 keeps the contradiction.
findings.evidence: weeks/week-06-evaluation-1.md:527 "(the layer-5 traces)"; weeks/week-05-control-safety-reliability.md 5.5 'The idea': "This is layer 6 (feedback and evals), with hooks into every other layer."; 7.1 now says 5.5 "is also part of layer 6".
findings.proposed_change: Replace "(the layer-5 traces)" with "(the traces 5.5 set up, also layer 6)" or simply drop the parenthetical. Grep weeks/ for "layer-5 traces" and "layer-5 observability" to confirm no other copy remains.

findings.checklist_item: A. Contradictions between lessons; Plain language: simplifying must not change meaning
findings.title: Week 5 review overstates 5.4: "beat every published detector" vs "most of 12 defences"
findings.claim: The review paragraph says adaptive attacks "beat every published detector". The lesson body says the authors bypassed most of 12 defences more than 90% of the time, and that it was human red-teamers who beat every defence. The new In short (line 423) correctly says "most published defences", so the file now contradicts itself. The PR description flags this as a possible email error left as written.
findings.evidence: weeks/week-05-control-safety-reliability.md:423 "adaptive attacks got past most published defences"; :430 "They bypassed most of them more than 90% of the time, and human red-teamers ... beat every defence"; :862 "adaptive attacks beat every published detector". Source: The Attacker Moves Second (Oct 2025), https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.09023, 12 defences tested.
findings.proposed_change: In the review paragraph write: "adaptive attacks got past most published defences, and human red-teamers beat all of them". Since this is a faithful carry-over from the email, the alternative is a short editorial note rather than a silent change; owner's call.

findings.checklist_item: Visuals: does the diagram match the text?
findings.title: error-two-paths sends every in-tool failure through "retry inside the tool"
findings.claim: The only edge out of "inside a tool" is TR "Infra error: retry inside the tool", so a task error (bad site code, crashed script) appears to be retried before it becomes an error result. The lesson says task errors must go straight back to the model and that retrying a bad tool call is the beginner's mistake. The alt text at week-02 line 778 adds the condition "if it is an infrastructure error", but the picture does not.
findings.evidence: error-two-paths.mmd: F -->|"inside a tool"| TR["Infra error: retry inside the tool"] --> TE. Lesson 2.6: "Task errors ... The model must see these"; "The beginner's mistake ... retrying a bad tool call three times".
findings.proposed_change: Add a decision node after "inside a tool": {"Infra glitch?"} with yes → TR (retry inside the tool) and no → TE (error result). Re-render with python3 tools/render_diagrams.py error-two-paths and update the alt text to match.

findings.checklist_item: Visuals: do not set colours in the file; classDef for at most two highlight styles
findings.title: course-map uses three coloured classDefs; STYLE allows at most two
findings.claim: The course map defines three classDef styles (done, now, todo) with explicit fills, strokes and text colours. STYLE.md says not to set colours in the file and permits classDef for at most two highlight styles. Either the diagram should drop one style (todo can be the default) or STYLE.md should say status maps are an exception.
findings.proposed_change: Remove the todo classDef and let the shared config style those nodes, keeping done and now as the two highlights; or add one line to STYLE.md allowing a third status style for the course map. Re-render and check the README caption ("grey is still to come") still matches.

findings.checklist_item: Lesson template: In short bullets, "in one line"
findings.title: Several In short bullets run to 30–40 words and two clauses
findings.claim: The template asks for the main idea, why it matters and the one thing to do, each in one line. Some bullets pack a whole procedure in: 7.1 line 20 (four steps), 1.3 line 283, 1.4 line 432, 4.5 line 604, 6.1 line 28, 2.3 line 303. On a phone these wrap to three or four lines and read like the body, not a summary.
findings.evidence: grep '^> - .{150,}' weeks/ returns 11 bullets, 6 of them in files this PR changed.
findings.proposed_change: Trim each to one clause, e.g. 7.1: "Reading a failed transcript is a four-step procedure, not skimming." Keep the steps in the body. Check with: grep -nE '^> - .{150,}' weeks/*.md returns nothing.

findings.checklist_item: Links: a link to the right file but the wrong lesson
findings.title: 4.4 says SWE-bench Lite is "covered in 6.6", but 6.6 covers SWE-bench Verified
findings.claim: The new gloss points the reader to 6.6 for SWE-bench Lite. 6.6's table and text describe SWE-bench Verified (500 issues) and never mention Lite, so the reader arrives and finds a different split.
findings.evidence: week-04 line 497; week-06 6.6 table row "SWE-bench (Verified) | 500 human-filtered GitHub issues".
findings.proposed_change: Write: "(SWE-bench Lite is a 300-task subset of SWE-bench, a coding benchmark; 6.6 covers the Verified split.)" or drop the link and keep only the one-line definition.

findings.checklist_item: Lesson template: Review days become a "Week N review" section with a short recap
findings.title: Recap heading differs across weeks after this pass
findings.claim: Week 2 renames its recap heading to "### Recap" (as Weeks 3 and 4 already do), while Weeks 1, 5 and 6 keep "### The week in six paragraphs", which is no longer accurate once the paragraphs are split into lists. No file links to either anchor, so nothing breaks, but the inconsistency is new in this PR.
findings.evidence: grep '^### Recap|^### The week in six' weeks/: Recap in weeks 2,3,4; six paragraphs in weeks 1,5,6.
findings.proposed_change: Use "### Recap" in all week reviews and add it to the STYLE.md template so the Saturday task follows it.
